payload.task_text:
Your procurement team must conduct a comprehensive supplier contract compliance audit to ensure vendors meet contractual obligations and to identify opportunities for improved performance. The first phase involves retrieving all active supplier contracts and service agreements. Organize contracts by supplier, service category, and contract start date. Create a central repository of all contract documents ensuring easy access and version control. Document basic information for each supplier including contact details, services provided, contract value, and renewal dates.

In the second phase, you will extract and document all key performance indicators and compliance requirements specified in each contract. For each supplier agreement, identify service level commitments such as delivery timelines, product quality standards, or customer support response times. Extract financial terms including pricing, payment terms, and volume discounts. Document any compliance requirements such as insurance, certifications, or regulatory approvals. Create a comprehensive matrix documenting all contractual obligations for each supplier.

The third phase requires monitoring actual service delivery against contractual commitments. For each supplier, gather performance data covering quality metrics, on-time delivery rates, responsiveness, and other relevant measures. Compare actual performance against the contractual performance standards. Identify areas where suppliers are exceeding expectations and areas where performance falls short of commitments. Document specific instances of non-compliance with supporting evidence.

In the fourth phase, you will create detailed compliance scorecards for each supplier. Calculate compliance scores for different performance dimensions. Present findings in visual formats showing which suppliers are meeting obligations and which require attention. Create trend analyses showing whether supplier performance is improving or deteriorating over time. Aggregate compliance data across all suppliers to identify organization-wide patterns.

The fifth phase involves conducting detailed root cause analysis for performance gaps. Determine whether failures to meet contractual obligations result from supplier capability issues, insufficient resources, external factors, or unclear expectations. Assess the business impact of non-compliance and prioritize issues for remediation. Develop specific, actionable recommendations for improving supplier performance.

The sixth phase requires drafting comprehensive audit findings and reports. Document all compliance findings with supporting evidence and impact assessments. Present findings in professional audit report format with executive summary, detailed findings, and recommendations. Send audit reports to suppliers and business stakeholders through email. Include specific remediation requirements with deadline expectations. Schedule meetings with underperforming suppliers to develop improvement plans with clear accountability and monitoring mechanisms.

## Deliverables

Produce the following files in your workspace (`supplier_list.csv` in the workspace lists the five suppliers and their contact emails):

1. `compliance_assessment.xlsx` — a spreadsheet with one sheet named `Compliance Assessment`; one row per supplier with the compliance dimension scores and an overall compliance score per supplier.
2. `corrective_actions.xlsx` — a spreadsheet with one sheet named `Corrective Actions`; rows listing, for each supplier, the identified issue, the required remediation action, an owner, a target date, an estimated cost, and a status.
3. `audit_findings.docx` — a Word document with the detailed audit findings: per-supplier gaps, risk levels, supporting evidence, and impact assessments.
4. `audit_summary.docx` — a Word document with the executive summary: overall compliance status, key findings, and strategic recommendations.
5. `compliance_report.pdf` — the full compliance audit report in professional format (executive summary, detailed findings, and recommendations).

Finally, send the audit report by email to the supplier contacts in `supplier_list.csv` (reach at least two suppliers) — use a subject that references the audit or compliance review — and schedule a follow-up meeting on the calendar with each underperforming supplier.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two dependency waves: one evidence-collector/dataset-builder keeps the heavy inventory out of the main context and freezes ONE canonical audit dataset (audit_data.json), then three artifact owners run in parallel from that single data source; emails and calendar stay with the main agent. Preserve evidence limitations instead of inventing contracts or performance history.

Before Wave 1, the main agent starts from supplier_list.csv and probes the two capability questions once: confirm whether the granted warehouse contains any supplier-specific contract/performance source, and probe ReportLab / exposed headless-Chromium PDF creation once, retaining the first genuine available path.

Wave 1 — dispatch coder 0 (office-report-builder 0), the evidence collector and dataset builder. It dynamically locates and reads every task-visible input (starting from supplier_list.csv, then inventorying every other workspace source and inspecting its content before deciding whether it is an executed agreement, a generic template, performance evidence, configuration/context, or irrelevant), searches the granted Snowflake schemas for supplier/contract/performance tables, and writes ONE runtime-unique audit_data.json in the task workspace covering all five supplier rows — separately recording identity/contact/service/value/start-date evidence, any generic obligations discovered, any genuinely supplier-specific contract/performance evidence, and missing fields such as renewal, SLA, dated trend, owner, target date and cost — together with metadata, findings, corrective actions, trends, aggregate counts and an executive summary derived only from that evidence, using a clearly labeled Evidence Not Available / Review Required status and a documented neutral scoring convention when no supplier-specific performance exists. It must not call a generic document an executed agreement, infer non-compliance from missing evidence, or fabricate trends, breaches, renewal dates, costs, or root causes. Return only path/hash/schema/control counts and a compact evidence/limitation summary; keep all parsing and dataset assembly inside this agent (it may script locally, but must not spawn agents).

After Wave 1, the main agent validates five-supplier coverage and the packet hash, and freezes the verified audit_data.json path as the sole downstream source.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel in one response, each consuming ONLY audit_data.json:

1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): The sole spreadsheet writer creates both `compliance_assessment.xlsx` and `corrective_actions.xlsx`. The first has one `Compliance Assessment` row per supplier with at least Supplier, dimension scores/statuses, Overall Score, and evidence notes. The second has one `Corrective Actions` row per supplier with Issue, Remediation Action, Owner, Target Date, Estimated Cost, and Status; use evidence-collection remediation for unknowns without pretending unknown performance is a breach. Prefer generating both workbooks in one script execution (openpyxl) and read both complete ranges back once each.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): The sole document writer creates both `audit_findings.docx` and `audit_summary.docx` with python-docx in ONE script execution — build the complete content of both files in a single local python run and write them in one pass, never issuing per-heading/per-paragraph Word MCP calls. The findings document covers every supplier, evidence, gaps, risks, impacts, and recommendations; the distinct summary contains the required executive sections and explicit source limitations. Read both documents back once each.
3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 2): The sole PDF writer uses the retained genuine ReportLab or headless-Chromium path to create `compliance_report.pdf` (not renamed text/HTML), including a supplier matrix, findings, actions, recommendations, and limitations, building it in one script execution where possible. Use the PDF tools to extract the completed PDF once to verify page count and required sections.

Every artifact owner self-verifies before returning. After the wave, the main agent requires all five file receipts and successful PDF text extraction. Resolve the verified `compliance_report.pdf` absolute path only from that receipt. Select exactly two contacts from `supplier_list.csv` by descending annual contract value with supplier-name tie-break. In one native-parallel batch, exhaust Sent searches for each exact recipient plus deterministic supplier-specific audit/compliance subject; send each missing message at most once with only that supplier's evidence status and the verified PDF attached, never retry an ambiguous send, then read both retained messages back. No email may start before the PDF receipt exists, and no message may expose another supplier's address.

For calendar follow-up, do not relabel `Evidence Not Available` as verified underperformance, but treat its missing contract/performance documentation as an actionable compliance-evidence gap. Choose the single evidence-gap supplier with highest annual contract value, breaking ties by supplier name. Use a task-visible meeting schedule when present; otherwise derive the first conflict-free weekday at least seven days after launch at 10:00-10:30 in the environment timezone. Call list_events(timeMin=<start ISO>, timeMax=<end ISO>, maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime"), inspect the exact title/time locally, and create only an absent event with summary="Supplier Compliance Evidence Review - <Supplier Name>", matching start/end.dateTime plus timeZone, and the supplier contact/requested evidence in description; retrieve the retained event ID. The main agent then checks five-supplier coverage, packet consistency, exactly two separate supplier recipients, all file receipts, and the supplier-specific event receipt; no second agent wave, duplicate writer, or repair agent is allowed.

Plan this end-to-end supplier contract compliance audit. Workspace is strictly /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-supplier-contract-compliance-audit/workspace. Need inspect available files read-only and propose concrete decomposition, evidence sources, underperformance logic, artifact validation, email and calendar actions. Deliverables: compliance_assessment.xlsx, corrective_actions.xlsx, audit_findings.docx, audit_summary.docx, compliance_report.pdf; email report to at least two supplier contacts from supplier_list.csv; meetings with every underperforming supplier. Do not write or mutate. Return exact relevant file paths found, key risks, and recommended execution/verification sequence.
Plan supplier audit workflow

Create all five required deliverables in /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-supplier-contract-compliance-audit/workspace using the available local Office tools. Inputs: supplier_list.csv and contract_template.pdf in that folder; data.csv is unrelated placeholder and must not be used as supplier evidence. Deliver exactly: (1) compliance_assessment.xlsx with exactly one sheet named 'Compliance Assessment', one row per all five suppliers, dimension scores and overall score; (2) corrective_actions.xlsx with exactly one sheet named 'Corrective Actions', rows per supplier covering identified issue, remediation, owner, target date, estimated cost, status; (3) audit_findings.docx with detailed per-supplier gaps, risk, evidence, impact; (4) audit_summary.docx with overall compliance status, key findings, strategic recommendations; (5) compliance_report.pdf as a polished full report with executive summary, detailed findings and recommendations. Important evidence constraints: only standard contract_template.pdf exists, not executed supplier-specific agreements; no attributable supplier performance data exists. Do not fabricate actual KPI results or contract breaches. Use template requirements (99.5% uptime, 4h response, 24h critical resolution, net 30, PO and itemization, $2M insurance, applicable laws, 12mo renewable, 60d convenience/15d cause, confidentiality 3 years, IP terms) as provisional criteria only. Rate every supplier 'Underperforming – Compliance Assurance Deficient / Not Assessed' because missing executed agreements and performance/compliance evidence prevent assurance, not because a breach was proven. Create transparent scoring: Contract Documentation 20, Performance Evidence 0, Financial Compliance Evidence 0, Insurance/Regulatory Evidence 0, Governance/Reporting 20, overall weighted 8/100 (equal-weight dimensions), Evidence Coverage 0%, for each supplier. Clearly label this as provisional evidence-readiness score, not actual service performance. Use source supplier details and contract values. Corrective actions: at least 3 per supplier (provide executed agreement/amendments, provide prior 12 months KPI/service evidence, provide financial/insurance/regulatory evidence), with supplier contact as owner, reasonable target dates 10/20/30 calendar days from current date, reasonable estimated audit/remediation costs, Open status. Include root-cause hypotheses (records unavailable/not centralized, reporting feed not provided) clearly marked to validate; impacts and risk levels. Add score visualization(s) and comparison/trend note: trend unavailable due no time-series. Professional formatting. Produce PDF by converting a polished full-report DOCX source if helpful, but final required five files must exist. Validate workbook sheet names, row counts, document readability, PDF page count. Return artifact paths and validation results.
Build audit deliverables

Execute authorized external actions for supplier audit. Workspace is strictly /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-supplier-contract-compliance-audit/workspace. Read supplier_list.csv and use compliance_report.pdf at exact path in that folder. All five suppliers are provisionally categorized 'Underperforming – Compliance Assurance Deficient / Not Assessed' due missing executed agreements and performance/compliance evidence; no actual breach is proven. (1) Send a separate personalized email to EACH of the five supplier contact emails (at minimum two must succeed), subject containing 'Supplier Contract Compliance Audit' and supplier name. Attach compliance_report.pdf. Explain provisional 8/100 evidence-readiness score and 0% evidence coverage, not actual service-performance score. Require: executed agreement/amendments in 10 calendar days, prior 12 months KPI/service evidence in 20 days, and financial/insurance/regulatory evidence in 30 days; ask acknowledgment and named owner. (2) Schedule a separate 60-minute follow-up meeting for EACH of the five suppliers. Choose reasonable future business-day slots, non-conflicting based on calendar, within 10 business days, timezone UTC unless calendar indicates otherwise. Invite that supplier's contact email. Title 'Corrective Action Review – [Supplier] – Supplier Contract Compliance Audit'. Description must include provisional status, agenda to confirm evidence gaps/root causes/actions/owners/milestones/closure evidence, and the 10/20/30 calendar-day requirements. Return exact email recipients/subjects and success/message identifiers if available, plus calendar event IDs/start/end/attendees. Verify via read-back where possible. Do not send any other files.
Send reports schedule meetings
